sources.verified: Opened final published HTML: Introduction dates implementation to 2017; Methods specifies 15 villages in Keonjhar and Jharsuguda and 2019–20 camp cycles. Discussion explicitly denies causal inference, citing nonrandom allocation, pandemic disruption and follow-up limitations. Programme-affiliated coauthor is visible.
sources.safe_text: A 2019–20 evaluation in 15 villages in Keonjhar and Jharsuguda associated the camps with reduced malaria infection. Its authors cautioned that the study could not establish causality. This evaluates the programme, not the film’s effects.

sources.verified: Opened publisher page and PDF text. Methods names five districts excluding Malkangiri; 53 workers interviewed. Theme3 supports roads, camp scheduling, staffing and supply constraints; p62 supports volunteer follow-up incentives. Contributions identify programme staff collecting interviews.
sources.safe_text: Interviews published in 2025 with 53 health workers described difficult roads, staff and supply shortages, and inconvenient camp schedules. Respondents sought support for volunteers’ work between camps. These are workers’ accounts from five districts outside Malkangiri, not a survey of residents or film audiences.

chronology.safe_text: Government reporting records funding approved for 2016–17, while the published evaluation dates implementation to 2017. Neither date should be confused with the film’s 2015 setting.
